newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian April crude/condensate output rate up.
newsitem.headline: Australian April crude/condensate output rate up.

text.p: Production of Australian crude oil and condensate in April was 2,592 megalitres or 544,000 barrels per day, a daily rate 3.4 percent higher than in April 1996, Department of Primarty Industries and Energy (DPIE) figures show.

For the first 10 months of fiscal 1996/97 (July/June) crude and condensate production increased 3.6 percent and naturally occurring liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) increased 3.5 percent the same period a year earlier, DPIE said.
Output of ethane declined 8.0 percent and natural gas production fell 2.5 percent over the same period, it said.
Total petroleum product sales in April 1997 rose 3.7 percent to 3,705.9 megalitres from 3,616.5 in April 1996.
However, sales volume remained about the same at 43,060.2 megalitres for the 10-month year-to-date comparison between 1995/96 and 1996/97, it said.
There was an increase of 5.2 percent in exports of petroleum in April 1997 over April 1996.
Australian exports of petroleum in April 1997 were 1,999.4 megalitres, of which 1,207.3 megalitres was crude oil and other refinery feedstocks and 299.9 megalitres was LPG.
Australian imports of petroleum in April 1997 were 2,210.2 megalitres, which was 18.6 percent below the April 1996 figure, DPIE said.
Over 90 percent (2,006.8 megalitres) of petroleum imports was crude oil and other refinery feedstocks, it said.
For two-way trade in petroleum and fiscal (10-month) year-to-date comparison, Australian petroleum exports are growing at a faster rate (16.0 percent) than petroleum imports (5.1 percent), DPIE said.
